chunks: It was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Abū al-Qāsim Saʿīd ibn Muḥammad al-Kūfī, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from ʿĪṣ, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man dies while he is in a state of janabah? He said: He is washed for janabah, then he is washed afterward with the ghusl of the dead.

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: The state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl.
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: A person in a state of major ritual impurity due to janabah.
key_terms.غُسْلَ الْمَيِّتِ: The ritual washing of the deceased.
key_terms.يُغْسَلُ: He is to be washed ritually.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person dies while in a state of janabah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who dies while in a state of janabah. It indicates that the deceased is first washed for janabah and then washed with the ghusl of the dead, showing the juridical treatment of overlapping ritual states at death.
